title: Slice-based capacity signals and rollout dependency plan for Private deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Plan and sequence a slice-driven rollout for Private/VPC/on-prem enterprise deployments that ties capacity signals, upgrade windows, and cross-team dependencies to measurable OKRs. Deliverables: a rollout sequencing matrix, gating criteria, capacity-signal definitions (traffic, KV cache hit rates, per-tenant latency percentiles), communication/playbook for customer success and SRE, and a list of automated dashboards and alerts needed before canary and broad rollouts.
comments: 2026-01-20 - Kickoff: alignment with SRE, Dedicated infra, and Sales engineering. Agreed on three rollout slices: pilot customers (<5 tenants), early adopters (5-25), general availability (>25).
2026-01-28 - Design review with DES: UX for upgrade windows and tenant opt-in flows needs tie-in to Console feature flags (DES-204 assigned).
2026-02-03 - Engineering feasibility: ENG-4923 to expose per-tenant KV cache metrics; ENG-5010 to add autoscaling headroom metrics. Both marked blocker for canary.
2026-02-12 - Legal/compliance: require checklist for encrypted backups and KMS key rotation before slice 2. Added as gating criteria.
2026-02-20 - PM review: consolidated gating criteria and drafted comms template. Plan moved to In Progress; next is dashboard ownership handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Gating matrix completed and reviewed by SRE/infra/CS; sign-off recorded in Confluence
Automated dashboards created: per-tenant p50/p95 latency, KV cache hit ratio, token/sec per-tenant, and error-rate; alerts with runbook attached
Canary run executed with pilot slice (3 tenants) for two weeks with no critical incidents and <10% latency regression on p95
Upgrade window flow integrated in Console behind feature flag and validated in a staging Private cluster
Customer success templates and rollback playbook published in Drive and linked in this ticket
decisions: Adopt slice boundaries by tenant count instead of revenue for first two quarters to simplify telemetry and membership checks
Require both KV cache hit ratio > 40% and p95 latency delta < 15% as quantitative gating signals for expanding slices
Use feature-flagged upgrade windows in Console to allow opt-in per-tenant during slice 2 rollout
next_steps: ENG: finish ENG-4923 (per-tenant KV metrics) by 2026-02-28
SRE: create Grafana dashboard panels and alert rules; schedule handoff workshop 2026-02-25
DES: validate upgrade modal copy and rollback confirmation flows in staging by 2026-03-05
PM: prepare customer comms and internal runbook; coordinate pilot tenants with Sales Eng
metrics: OKR-PD-1: Reduce private-deploy p95 latency regression vs baseline <= 12% during rollout
OKR-PD-2: Achieve automated canary sign-off cadence of <= 14 days for pilot slice
Operational: per-tenant KV cache hit rate, per-tenant tokens/sec, error rate (5xx)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Insufficient telemetry leads to late detection of regressions. Mitigation: block canary until ENG-4923 and ENG-5010 are complete and dashboards are validated.
Risk: Legal/compliance delays for specific customers. Mitigation: create a compliance gating checklist and escalate customers through Enterprise success early in slice planning.
Risk: Upgrade windows conflict with customer SLAs. Mitigation: offer out-of-hours scheduling and opt-in dry-run capability before committing to major changes.
